To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the composition of the prokaryotes in deep waters of the Atlantic Ocean is depth stratified and that the pro karyotic community of North Atlantic Deep Water undergoes successional change in this conduit between western and eastern Atlantic basins.

the prokayotic community of the North Atlantic deep water changes in a conduit between the western to the eastern Atlantic basin, and that the community of the Antarctic Bottom Water, the deepest layer, is dominated by archaea.

the composition of bacterial and archaea in the water masses of the Romanche Fracure Zone (RF2) was depth stratified, with a significant increase in Thaumarchaea in the deepest water mass (Antartic Bottom Water, ABBW).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the composition of the bacterial and archaea communities in distinct water masses in the deep sea, their distribution with depth, their spatial distribution along the RFZ and their successional changes within a water mass during its passage through the conduit.
the composition and distribution of prokaryotes in the deep ocean and their response to environmental changes.
the spatial distribution of prokaryotes in the deep ocean and the succession of their communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prokayotic community is depth-stratified and that the community composition of the NADWP changes with a passage time of 4 months.
the prokayotic community of the water masses is not static but dynamic and that it is affected by the physical properties of the water masses and the time spent in the water mass.
the prokarian community of the NAWD undergoes successional change within a time frame comparable to that of surface water prokarian communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prokaryotic diversity is not a function of the depth but of the physical and chemical properties of the water masses.
the bacterial community of the NABW undergoes successsional changes in this conduits between the western and easten Atlantic basin.
bacterial and archaeal assemblages in the deep ocean are more diverse than previously thought, and that they respond to subtle changes in their habitat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prokayotic communities are not static, but rather dynamic and that the community composition changes with time and space.
the composition of the prokaryote community changes in the NADW as it passes through the RFZ, which is an important pathway for deep-water exchange between the eastern and western Atlantic.
the prokarya of the deep sea are not just ‘dead’ and that they respond to changes in the environment, albeit at a much slower pace than in the surface ocean.
